page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.4-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. Configured with 4 physical cores and simultaneous multithreading enabled at two threads per core, it presents 8 dedicated vCPUs to the guest operating system alongside 32.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

The virtual machine does not include bundled local disk storage or hardware-based GPU accelerators. Persistent data persistence requires external network-attached block storage volumes. Network connectivity features one complimentary public IPv4 address provisioned alongside the instance interface.

With its dedicated core scheduling and balanced allocation of compute and system memory, VM.Standard.E6.Flex.4-32 provides consistent runtime performance without resource contention from shared-core burst models. The balanced resource footprint delivers predictable cost efficiency for continuous workloads, including mid-tier application backends, container orchestration nodes, relational databases, continuous integration tasks, and web serving.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.4-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on x86_64 AMD EPYC 9J45 processors operating at 2.7 GHz. It allocates 4 physical cores and 8 dedicated vCPUs with 2 threads per core, paired with 32.0 GB of RAM to deliver a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. The instance contains zero discrete GPUs and provides no integrated local disk storage, necessitating remote block storage attachments for persistent filesystem needs. Network provisioning includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Featuring dedicated CPU execution rather than burstable or shared allocations, VM.Standard.E6.Flex.4-32 delivers consistent processing capacity suited for standard business systems, web applications, microservices hosting, database engines, and continuous integration pipelines.
